Q: Python Regex for a closing parenthesis without an opening parenthesis A:

This simple regex uses an alternation that defines two premises:

  1. Match a string that has an open paren ( that does not have a closing paren ) downstream.
  2. Match a string that has close paren ) that does not have an open ( paren upstream.

After a bit of factoring, the regex is.
Assumes each line is self contained.

(?m)^[^(\r\n]*(?:\([^)\r\n]*|\).*)$

https://regex101.com/r/Ys4pkN/1

(?m)                             # Multiline
^                                # BOL
[^(\r\n]*                        # Not (
(?:
   \( [^)\r\n]*                  #  ( .....
 |                               # or
   \) .*                         #  ..... )
)
$                                # EOL

This does not address balancing. Only these two simple premises.

Q: What does constitute one character for regcomp? Which multibyte encoding does determine this? A:

Each Unicode codepoint constitutes a “character” for this purpose, even in a multi-byte encoding such as UTF-8. POSIX-2024 specifies (emphasis added):

Regular expressions are a context-independent syntax that can represent a wide variety of character sets and character set orderings, where these character sets are interpreted according to the current locale.

The Base Definitions say that a UTF-8 codepoint (if supported) counts as a single “character”:

A sequence of one or more bytes representing a member of a character set. [...]

This term [“character”] corresponds to the ISO C standard term multi-byte character

The document this references, ISO/IEC 9899:2023, defines “multibyte character” as a

sequence of one or more bytes representing a member of the extended character set [...]

Where the “extended character set” is ISO 10646/Unicode or some superset of it.

The specification of Regular Expressions (linked above) then says of the bracket expression you were asking about:

A bracket expression (an expression enclosed in square brackets, "[]") is an RE that shall match a specific set of single characters, and may match a specific set of multi-character collating elements, based on the non-empty set of list expressions contained in the bracket expression.

And:

When a multi-character collating element in a bracket expression is involved, the longest sequence shall be measured in characters consumed from the string to be matched; that is, the collating element counts not as one element, but as the number of characters it matches.

The example given of a collating element was a ch ligature used to sort strings in Spanish alphabetical order.

Character classes are additionally specified to follow LC_CTYPE categories. If you call setlocale( LC_ALL, "" ), the LC_ALL environment variable overrides LC_CTYPE, which overrides LANG. Therefore, if you want to set any category individually, such as LC_TIME or LC_NUMERIC, you need to set the LANG variable, which is the default for all other categories, rather than LC_ALL, which overrides all other setttings. It makes no sense to combine UTF-8 and non-UTF-8 locale categories (which might produce invalid UTF-8 strings). Therefore, you would normally export LANG to a UTF-8 locale, one or more categories to a different UTF-8 locale, and never need to set LC_CTYPE or LC_ALL.

The language[_territory][.codeset] format for locale names is recommended by POSIX and supported by GNU libc. Lowercase ISO 639 language codes and uppercase two-letter ISO 3166 territory codes are the de facto standard. Mainstream OSes including Windows 10 and 11 now understand ru_RU.UTF-8. However, the locale might or might not be installed at runtime, so you should check the return value of setlocale(LC_ALL, "") for error, and might want to fall back on en_US.UTF-8, which should also work for this purpose, if that fails.

Since it is possible for the user to select a non-UTF-8 locale, you may want to check for this as well. On Linux (and most UNIX dialects), you can test

strcmp(nl_langinfo(CODESET), "UTF-8") == 0

Windows 10/11 allows you to set the locale to ".UTF-8", for the user’s preferred language and settings along with the UTF-8 character set.

The GNU C library documents some very minor differences in section 7.6 of its manual.. These should not be visible to your application.

Q: Supabase error new row violates row-level security policy for table A:

For anyone that's using spuabase for the 1st time like I am. I stumbled into the same error. You have to create a policy for every command(insert, update, etc.) that's being used of each table. That can be done going into Authentication>Configuration>Policies>Create Policy(upper right corner of the table card)

If you're just playing around with supabase, it'll make things much easier for you if you leave the target role empty. That's not secure so in a more enterprise product please don't leave it empty.

Q: Matching consecutive duplicate characters in a string in Google Sheets A:

Split the string into characters and check each individually, like this:

=let(
  text, A2,
  chars, arrayformula(mid(text, sequence(len(text)), 1)),
  textjoin(, true,
    filter(vstack(chars,), vstack(chars,) <> vstack(,chars))
  )
)

See let(), arrayformula(), sequence(), textjoin(), filter() and vstack().

Q: Typescript Exclude/Ignore (do not compile) File in rootDir A:

Here's what I did to achieve the goal.

In the following example, I want to compile all files in the src/ directory, except one (exclude.ts).

The set up:


├── node_modules
│   └── typescript
├── package.json
├── package-lock.json
├── src
│   ├── exclude.ts
│   └── include.ts
└── tsconfig.json

My tsconfig.json

{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "forceConsistentCasingInFileNames": true,
    "module": "commonjs",
    "outDir": "dist",
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "strict": true,
    "target": "es2016"
  },
  "exclude": [
    "src/exclude.ts"
  ],
  "include": [
    "src/"
  ]
}

This works. When I run the TypeScript compiler, I only see the include.js file in the dist/ directory. I thought I tried it before (as I state in my earlier question), but I must have missed something.

Q: Postman Request body data from Excel / CSV file - forward slash A:

I had similar issue with postman and realized my problem was more of a syntax issue.

Lets say your cvs file has the following columns:

        userId |    mid    | platform | type | ...etc
row1    94J4J  | 209444894 |   NORTH  |  PT  | ...
row2    324JE  | 934421903 |   SOUTH  |  MB  | ...
row3    966RT  | 158739394 |   EAST   |  PT  | ...

This is how you want your json request body to look like:

  {
    "userId" : "{{userId}}",
       "mids":[{
              "mid":"{{mid}}",
         "platform":"{{platform}}"
               }],
       "type":["{{type}}"],
        .. etc   
   }

Make sure your colums names match the varibales {{variableName}}
